newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end a shade lower in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end a shade lower in dull trade.

text.p: Profit-taking by speculators and financial institutions pushed share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange to a modestly lower close on Thursday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 0.93 point lower at 828.33 points.
"Selling by domestic financial institutions and squaring of positions by speculators mainly arrested the rally in share prices," said Manoj Aggarwal of brokers Multiple Investments.

Share prices have jumped by almost 12 percent since Finance Minister P. Chidambaram slashed taxes and announced measures considered friendly by the stock markets in his budget for 1997/98 (April-March) last Friday.
Brokers said investors tightened their positions ahead of Friday's holiday.
The Delhi Stock Exchange will remain closed on Friday for the Hindu festival Mahashivratri, bourse officials said.
Traders said the fall in share prices was temporary in nature and market was expected to stage another rally on Monday.
"Share prices have not reached their peaks, they will rise further," said another broker.
Reliance Industries fell 1.35 rupees to 301.70 as speculators squared positions, brokers said.
State Bank of India dropped 2.75 rupees to 324.50.
TELCO rose 10.50 rupees to 409.50 on strong buying by foreign institutional investors (FIIs), brokers said.
ACC gained 51.90 rupees to 1,851.90 on FII buying.
